items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: she wrote an article in Downbeat and said the trombone player was atrocious... I said, well, Helen, you were right.

ctx.x: I thought of -- I just tried. And naturally, it all ain't going to come out. So, I guess she came there one of those nights when it wasn't working, and she -- she wrote an article in Downbeat and said the trombone player was atrocious. And she probably was right, you know. I had to laugh about that thing, but it hurt me so bad at that time until I think I started practicing about eight hours a day after she wrote that.

I really went to practicing then. I said I'm not going to let this chick write like -- about me like that. And I just really. So, Earl and Stanley, they kid Helen when they want to kid her now. They say oh don't say nothing. You're the one that put Trummy down (unintelligible). And we were laughing about that a few days ago out there at Colorado, you know.

I said, well, Helen, you were right. I was kind of bad because I was just experimenting. And it happens to a guy who's taking chances. It's going to happen to you. It's like a ball player, you know. The guys who make the most errors are the guys who take the greatest chances. You're going to make errors if you take chances. But I was that kind. I was a gambler, you know, with that horn. I just took chances.
